source.title: Grokking as Compression: A Nonlinear Complexity Perspective
source.authors: Zi-Ming Liu; Zi-Qian Zhong; Max Tegmark

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Main results are described in text and figures; exact plotted values are not stated.
record.tranche_reason: Measures a different complexity quantity, LMN, during grokking and reports how it relates to test loss on algorithmic tasks. This bears on the broad question of measured properties tracking generalization, but not on the specific versions’ natural-image, optimizer, batch-size, regularization, or magnitude-aware-sharpness claims.
record.gate_note: The experiments use algorithmic tasks rather than natural data and do not test the listed version-specific interventions. Figure 2 reports training/test accuracy, LMN, and L2 trajectories; the text describes trends but gives no exact plotted values.
record.test_reason: The study measures linear mapping number (LMN) during grokking on three algorithmic tasks. None of V1–V8 concerns this measure or comparison. In particular, LMN is not magnitude-aware weight sharpness (V7), and its double-descent-like trajectory over training is not test error versus width (V2). Citing V7's original source does not test V7.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors interpret declining LMN as compression before generalization and describe its relation to test loss as more linear than that of L2 norm. They tentatively attribute XOR's later LMN increase to switching between asymmetric and symmetric solutions; this mechanism remains unverified. Broader applicability is proposed for future testing.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures LMN and L2 during grokking on algorithmic tasks, rather than testing the listed natural-data interventions or magnitude-aware sharpness.
record.method_sensitivity: For modular addition, only the first hidden layer is described as sensitive to hidden progress; the embedding and second hidden layers are less meaningful.

fits_no_version.finding: First-hidden-layer LMN decreases between memorization and generalization on three algorithmic tasks and is described as more linearly related to test loss than parameter L2 norm. XOR subsequently shows a temporary LMN increase, with turning points at 15 and 20.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LMN can track compression during grokking in the tested algorithmic networks, with a nonmonotonic post-generalization trajectory for XOR.

fits_no_version.finding: In modular addition, first-hidden-layer LMN captures progress before generalization; embedding- and second-hidden-layer LMN plateau soon after memorization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LMN's sensitivity to progress before grokking depends on which layer is measured.

record.problems: The experiments cover three algorithmic tasks and one network architecture and optimizer setup, not natural data. Exact plotted values and uncertainty estimates are not reported in the text. The proposed explanation for XOR is speculative and mechanistic investigation is deferred.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible results omitted. Figure 2 and Figure 3 contain plotted trajectories without exact values in the text; rows preserve the textual descriptions and do not reconstruct numbers.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting compared with natural-label held-out performance under the same architecture and recipe.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under specified tuning budgets and recovery recipes.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that reduce the penalty.
Dropout effects on held-out error and their dependence on data size, dropout strength, and augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness versus generalization gaps and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Test-accuracy effects of removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Algorithmic data alone would not exclude a study; the decisive issue is that its measurements and comparisons do not test any supplied version.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural labels.
Width sweep beyond interpolation on MNIST or downsampled CIFAR-10.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD on image or language benchmarks.
Large versus small batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons with norm- or margin-based measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.
